title: The Pawn Breakthrough
subtitle: Sacrifice two pawns to make the third one a queen.
goals: Calculate promotion races to the end
Sacrifice material for a passed pawn

steps.say: Three pawns against three, all blocked, kings far away — it looks like nothing. It is actually a forced win, and the mechanism is one of the most beautiful in chess: throw away TWO pawns so the third arrives at the queening square before anything can stop it. The whole thing is a counting exercise: if your pawn queens first by one move, you win.

steps.prompt: Three against three, all blocked. Find the breakthrough — the middle pawn goes first!
hints: The key is the MIDDLE pawn: it attacks both neighbours' recaptures at once, and whichever way Black takes, the other file opens.
b6! If axb6 then c6 runs; if cxb6 then a6 runs. Either way you queen first.

line.say: The sacrifice. Black must choose a side, and either capture opens a road...
The c-pawn is now unstoppable: c7 and c8=Q come next, and the black king is far too far away. You gave a pawn; you get a queen.
The middle pawn steps forward, offering itself to either neighbour...
The other side opens instead — and the a-pawn runs home unopposed. Symmetry is what makes the breakthrough work: whichever pawn takes, it abandons the file next door.

rejections.say: bxa6! and nothing runs: your remaining pawns are still blocked and you're a pawn down. The breakthrough only works with the MIDDLE pawn, because it deflects a defender either way.
bxc6 and the position is dead. Same reason: an outside pawn can be captured by a defender that stays in place. Push b6!
The king is far too slow to matter — this position is won by the pawns alone, right now. Count the race after b6! and you'll see the queen.

steps.wrongSay: One of the three pawns creates a passer whichever way Black captures. Which one?
steps.successSay: The 3-vs-3 breakthrough: memorize the picture and you'll spot it in real endings.

steps.prompt: You're Black, and the breakthrough has been played. Show the best defence — capture and run!
hints: You can't stop the passed pawn with the king, so grab material and count the race.
cxb6 keeps the pawn count even and forces White to prove the passer wins.

line.say: The most testing defence: take, and make White demonstrate. Now count the race with the a-file open — this is precisely the calculation you must do BEFORE allowing the breakthrough, not after.

rejections.say: The king is too slow — count the moves: the passer promotes long before he arrives. When facing a breakthrough, capture immediately and race; walking never works.

steps.wrongSay: Take the pawn and count the resulting race — that's the only defence worth trying.
steps.successSay: Both sides of the breakthrough understood: it's arithmetic, not magic.

steps.say: The transferable rule: whenever pawn majorities face each other with the kings out of range, look for the middle-pawn sacrifice. Two pawns for one queening pawn is always a bargain — and the defender's capture is what opens the very file you need.
